p.src: A Generator Kept in Reserve

u.src: A Generator Kept in Reserve
en: A Generator Kept in Reserve

p.src:
Before drawing a closed string, let us recover one fact from canonical mechanics. Suppose $L=L(q_i,\dot q_i),$ and define the momentum conjugate to $q_i$ by $p_i=\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot q_i}.$ An infinitesimal continuous transformation can be written $\delta q_i=\epsilon f_i(q),$ where $\epsilon$ is a small parameter. If this transformation is a symmetry, Noether’s theorem supplies a conserved charge. Dividing the coordinate displacement by the common parameter gives the generator $Q=\sum_i p_i f_i(q)
   =\frac{1}{\epsilon}\sum_i p_i\,\delta q_i.$ In quantum mechanics, $Q$ is the operator that generates the corresponding small transformation.

p.src: A closed string has no endpoints. Choose a parameter $0\leq \sigma<2\pi$ and, for the moment, mark one point as $\sigma=0$. p.src: Orientation had a concrete role in the original hadronic string picture. Breaking an oriented flux tube produces a quark at one endpoint and an antiquark at the other; the intrinsic arrow distinguishes the two ends. One can also construct unoriented string theories, but for the present discussion we retain the arrow and the two senses along it.

u.src: Periodicity and Running Waves
en: Periodicity and Running Waves

p.src:
Let $X(\sigma,\tau)$ and $Y(\sigma,\tau)$ be two transverse coordinates of the string, with $\tau$ denoting time. Extra transverse coordinates, when present, are treated in exactly the same way. Since $\sigma=0$ and $\sigma=2\pi$ label the same point, $X(\sigma+2\pi,\tau)=X(\sigma,\tau),
  \qquad
  Y(\sigma+2\pi,\tau)=Y(\sigma,\tau).$

p.src: A localized wiggle can therefore circulate indefinitely. When it reaches $2\pi$, it simply reappears at $0$. This differs from an open string, where a running wave reaches an endpoint and reflects; what was left-moving becomes right-moving and vice versa. Standing waves are natural for the open string, whereas a closed string admits two independently propagating families.

p.src:
The convenient basis for a periodic function is $e^{in\sigma}=\cos(n\sigma)+i\sin(n\sigma),
  \qquad n\in\mathbb Z.$ The integer condition is forced by periodicity: $e^{in(\sigma+2\pi)}=e^{in\sigma}$. Replacing $n$ by a half-integer, for example, would change the function after one circuit.

p.src:
Suppressing time dependence momentarily, the blackboard expansion is $\begin{aligned}
  X(\sigma)
  &=
  X_0+
  \sum_{n>0}X_n e^{in\sigma}
  +\sum_{n>0}X_{-n}e^{-in\sigma},
  \\
  Y(\sigma)
  &=
  Y_0+
  \sum_{n>0}Y_n e^{in\sigma}
  +\sum_{n>0}Y_{-n}e^{-in\sigma}.
  \end{aligned}$ For real $X$ and $Y$, the negative-index coefficients are complex conjugates of the positive-index coefficients at the classical level. The zero modes $X_0$ and $Y_0$ locate the center of mass; they are positions, not internal oscillations.

p.src: Thus it is the full phase, not the sign of $n$ in a purely spatial Fourier factor by itself, that determines propagation. We may write $X(\sigma,\tau)=X_R(\tau-\sigma)+X_L(\tau+\sigma),$ and similarly for $Y$. Which family is called $R$ rather than $L$ is a convention; the invariant fact is that there are two opposite directions along the $\sigma$-circle.

p.src: Energy in the Two Directions

u.src: Energy in the Two Directions
en: Energy in the Two Directions

p.src:
The local dynamics is the same as for the open string. In the simplified normalization used here, $L\propto
  \int_0^{2\pi}d\sigma\,
  \left[
    \dot X^2-X'^2+\dot Y^2-Y'^2
  \right],$ where a dot denotes $\partial_\tau$ and a prime denotes $\partial_\sigma$. The energy has a plus sign between kinetic and elastic terms: $E\propto
  \int_0^{2\pi}d\sigma\,
  \left[
    \dot X^2+X'^2+\dot Y^2+Y'^2
  \right].$ For either transverse coordinate, $\dot X^2+X'^2
  =
  \frac12(\dot X+X')^2+
  \frac12(\dot X-X')^2.$ The cross terms cancel, leaving precisely the original kinetic and gradient energies.

p.src:
For $X_R(\tau-\sigma)$, one has $\dot X_R=-X_R'$; for $X_L(\tau+\sigma)$, one has $\dot X_L=X_L'$. Consequently the two squares in  isolate the two chiral families. Including every transverse coordinate, define $\begin{aligned}
  E_L&\propto
  \frac12\int_0^{2\pi}d\sigma
  \sum_I(\dot X^I+X^{I\prime})^2,\\
  E_R&\propto
  \frac12\int_0^{2\pi}d\sigma
  \sum_I(\dot X^I-X^{I\prime})^2.
  \end{aligned}$ Then $E=E_L+E_R$. Because the equations are linear at this stage, waves from the two sectors pass through one another without scattering.

  \qquad
  \widetilde a_n^\dagger,\quad\widetilde b_n^\dagger,
  \qquad n>0.$ The untilded and tilded operators create opposite world-sheet directions; $a$ and $b$ denote the two transverse polarizations.

  \end{aligned}$ The ellipses stand for additional transverse directions.

p.src:
Recall the open-string first level. Acting on the ground state with $a_1^\dagger$ or $b_1^\dagger$ gives two linear polarizations. Their circular combinations, $c_\pm^\dagger
  =
  \frac{1}{\sqrt2}
  \left(a_1^\dagger\pm i b_1^\dagger\right),$ carry helicity $h=\pm1$. The absence of a helicity-zero partner is the signature of a massless vector in this elementary four-dimensional description.

p.src:
Let the closed-string ground state have mass squared $m_0^2$. A first, naive guess is to act once with any one of $a_1^\dagger,\quad b_1^\dagger,\quad
  \widetilde a_1^\dagger,\quad\widetilde b_1^\dagger.$ This resembles two copies of the open-string photon, one for each propagation direction. At the next energy, however, the unrestricted list does not assemble into sensible rotational multiplets. The problem is not repaired by more elaborate bookkeeping. The premise that every oscillator monomial is a physical state is wrong.

p.src:
Every state in  has one unit of energy in one sector and none in the other, so every one is excluded. The first surviving states carry one oscillator from each family: $\begin{aligned}
  a_1^\dagger\widetilde a_1^\dagger\ket{0},
  &\qquad
  b_1^\dagger\widetilde b_1^\dagger\ket{0},
  \\
  a_1^\dagger\widetilde b_1^\dagger\ket{0},
  &\qquad
  b_1^\dagger\widetilde a_1^\dagger\ket{0}.
  \end{aligned}$ They have total oscillator energy two, divided equally between the two directions. A single $n=2$ creation operator has the same total oscillator energy but fails ; it contributes two units to only one side.

p.src:
Regulate the loop as $M$ ordered points with transverse coordinates $(X_i,Y_i)$. Temporarily suppress $Y_i$. A configuration-space wavefunction is $\Psi(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_M).$ Changing which point is called first gives a cyclic permutation: $\begin{aligned}
  \Psi(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_M)
  &=
  \Psi(X_2,\ldots,X_M,X_1)\nonumber\\
  &=
  \Psi(X_3,\ldots,X_M,X_1,X_2).
  \end{aligned}$ This is not invariance under an arbitrary permutation. Inserting $X_3$ between $X_1$ and $X_2$, for example, changes the adjacency structure and effectively tears and reconnects the discretized string. Only the common cyclic relabeling $X_i\longrightarrow X_{i+1}\qquad(\text{mod }M)$ expresses the absence of a preferred origin.

In the coordinate representation, $P_X(\sigma)=-i\frac{\delta}{\delta X(\sigma)},
  \qquad
  P_Y(\sigma)=-i\frac{\delta}{\delta Y(\sigma)}$ with $\hbar=1$. Equation  is therefore generated by $G_\sigma=

    P_X(\sigma)X'(\sigma)+P_Y(\sigma)Y'(\sigma)

For the closed string, it leaves the graviton, the dilaton, the antisymmetric-tensor or axion-like state, and the higher matched levels.

p.src: The strongly coupled monopole also looks complicated from the electric description. Its field energy is large; it is dressed by an intense cloud of gauge-field fluctuations and virtual magnetically charged pairs. It behaves as a heavy, extended object, a poor starting point for an electric perturbation series. This does not prove that it is less fundamental. It says that it is the wrong elementary variable for that regime.

p.src: This ambiguity once surfaced in a discussion of whether the Higgs boson was fundamental or composite. Eugene Wigner repeatedly asked what composite meant. One proposed distinction was decay: perhaps a fundamental object cannot decay and a composite object can. But a ground-state hydrogen atom cannot decay and is plainly composite; the proton may be stable while the neutron decays, yet that does not make one elementary and the other composite in the intended sense. Every simple definition generated another counterexample.

p.src: Gerardus ’t Hooft ended the discussion with the operational criterion: an object is fundamental when it is useful to think of it as fundamental. This is not an evasion. It recognizes that elementary identifies the variables in which the dynamics is simple, and simplicity can depend on coupling and environment.

p.src: String theory realizes this exchange of roles in a particularly sharp way. In one parameter regime, strings are light and perturbative, while D-branes look like heavy solitonic composites built from string degrees of freedom. As the parameters change, D-branes can become the lighter elementary objects, and configurations described as strings in the first regime can be reinterpreted in terms of them. What looked fundamental can become composite; what looked composite can become fundamental.

u.src: String theory realizes this exchange of roles in a particularly sharp way. In one parameter regime, strings are light and perturbative, while D-branes look like heavy solitonic composites built from string degrees of freedom. As the parameters change, D-branes can become the lighter elementary objects, and configurations described as strings in the first regime can be reinterpreted in terms of them. What looked fundamental can become composite; what looked composite can become fundamental.
en: String theory realizes this exchange of roles in a particularly sharp way. As the parameters change, D-branes can become the lighter elementary objects, and configurations described as strings in the first regime can be reinterpreted in terms of them. What looked fundamental can become composite; what looked composite can become fundamental.

p.src: The old reductionist picture suggests a one-way descent from large things to smaller constituents and finally to a unique bottom layer. Duality suggests something less linear: descriptions can transform into one another as couplings vary, with no single set of variables privileged everywhere. That is the angle from which the next subject, M-theory, will be approached.

p.src: The questions of why the critical dimensions are twenty-six for the bosonic string and ten for the superstring remain open here. Rather than settling every technical issue before moving on, we now change viewpoint and ask how M-theory can produce string theory in an appropriate limit.
